correctness.rationale: Linear spatial operators and the order-two RK conditions give an identical primal update for every tableau. At gamma=1/2 a physical subcell partition gives a Jensen-based inequality for every convex entropy on exactly 0<=r<=1; r>1 is ruled out by constant-cell quadratic entropy. At gamma>1/2 a quartic hinge localized at the first-stage outflow yields a strictly negative exact defect for every r>0 and survives a positive quadratic addition producing a C2 strongly convex entropy. Exact checker validates the explicit -1/3072 witness and 320 formula instances. Alternating-mode determinant verifies the separate full-state amplification claim. No finite testing is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The compared primary studies establish cRKDG construction, invariant-region bound preservation, and a sufficiently dissipative uniformly strongly convex entropy inequality, but not a two-stage tableau rigidity result for arbitrary finite convex entropies with the RK-averaged upwind entropy flux. Our exact nonlinear entropy-flux aliasing obstruction survives even though all tableaus have the same linear primal update. Closest mathematical-record results concern other entropy and numerical stability problems and do not imply this claim; remaining unindexed literature risk is stated.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete natural RK2 design classification for entropy certificates: identical physical cRKDG solvers can differ categorically because of stagewise nonlinear entropy-flux quadrature. It supplies a sharp all-convex midpoint CFL, a smooth strongly convex obstruction for every non-midpoint tableau and every positive step, and a rigorous separation between cell-entropy budget and Fourier stability. These consequences inform selection of tableaux and interpretation of entropy checks and go beyond finite parameter recomputation.
